what_happened: The person running Athena queued a follow-up request that said a shared stand-in helper (for test scripts) already existed. No earlier try had landed it. They had seen a retry pass its checks and took that to mean it had landed, and they did not look at main. They closed the follow-up within a minute and queued it again with the correct premise. No job failed. This is an intervention note.
cause: Athena does not resolve a claim in a request that something from an earlier job exists against the current main. A job's state is easy to misread: "passed checks" on a try, "verified" and "landed" look alike in the job listing. The request writer is not shown whether a deliverable is on main. Nothing checks the request's premise before it is queued. The gap shows only when the reading or plan is built on something that is missing, or when the writer notices and closes the item.
prevention: At queue time, check each premise in a request that says an earlier job's file, helper or role already exists. Resolve each cited job id and named path against the current main snapshot. If a cited job has not landed, or a named item is not in main, refuse or warn with "job X has not landed; item Y is not on main". Show landed or not landed beside each job's state in the job listing, so passing checks cannot be read as landing.
proposed_request: When a request is queued, check every statement that an earlier job's deliverable already exists. For each job id or file path the request cites as existing, look it up in the current main snapshot and in the job's landed state. If the item is not on main, or the job has not landed, refuse the request at queue time with a message that names the job or path and says it is missing from main. Also show "landed" or "not landed" next to each job in the job listing. Acceptance: (1) a request citing a verified but unlanded job's helper is refused with that message; (2) a request citing a landed job's helper is accepted; (3) the listing shows landed or not landed for each job; (4) a test covers both cases using a snapshot built the way Athena builds real ones.
